paper_metadata.title: Predictors of long-term survival among first-ever ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke in a Brazilian stroke cohort

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a prospective, consecutive recruitment strategy from a well-defined geographical area (Butantan, São Paulo) with clear inclusion/exclusion criteria. The baseline characteristics are thoroughly described, and the use of a community hospital that handles 80% of local hospitalizations minimizes selection bias.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: The Hospital Universitário is located in the west area of the city of São Paulo... which includes 420,000 inhabitants.
items.reasoning: The authors define the geographical and demographic source of the population clearly.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: We prospectively ascertained 665 consecutive first-ever ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke cases... who were discharged after a first hospitalization for stroke at community hospital.
items.reasoning: Consecutive recruitment from a primary facility for the area reduces the risk of convenience sampling bias.

items.reasoning: The start and end dates are explicitly stated.

items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
